name: Harriet Ho
life: “I still remember the first time two employees offered one job a better shape.” Monday often includes a stop at the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, where Harriet checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I wanted to announce a winner. They came back with a split-shift proposal and asked me to cost it.
appearance: Harriet has a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Look for a dark undercut with a longer wave on top. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a washed violet jersey with a little coil of soft measuring tape. In conversation Harriet looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Harriet loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Harriet remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To get the two-shift proposal costed honestly.
family: Frances Ortiz is Harriet’s cousin. Harriet brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Frances makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The tide clock*, Frances says, “I fixed the minute hand before I knew it wasn't minutes.”
connections: Harley Kelly. The shift manager has to cost the proposal that upends a simple hiring contest.
